use_case_summary: Primary: regulated customer support assistant + document search for investor relations. Must keep PII in-region; embeddings used for search; periodic batch embeddings for nightly sync.
notes: High-level: FinServ analytics shop, heavy on compliance. Looking to run Redwood Private in VPC with strict egress controls. Very sensitive to keys and audit streams.

Network ask (detailed): prefer AWS PrivateLink interface endpoints over VPC peering due to cross-account isolation. Wants option A: interface endpoint + NLB with static IPs; option B: VPC peering + transit gateway if PrivateLink not feasible for throughput.

Firewall / Egress: corporate perimeter expects egress from Redwood to come from a small set of static IPs for allowlisting. Customer team will only open outbound ports to those IPs. Also need explicit support for restricting DNS and using internal resolvers (split-horizon).
IP allowlist: security requires allowlisting by CIDR and ASN where possible. Must provide certificate for each hostname and confirm TLS1.2+ and mTLS options for control-plane hooks.

NAT / Route tables: discuss NAT gateway vs egress-only LB. They prefer egress through customer-managed NAT so we should support configuring route tables or bringing our NAT in their VPC via PrivateLink.

Transit & peering constraints: central infra uses Transit Gateway; any VPC peering needs approval from network team. PrivateLink would simplify approvals but they want throughput numbers (max concurrent connections, Gb/s).

KMS integration: must support customer-managed CMK in AWS KMS (no external import). Key policies: Redwood must be able to use KMS key via grant, but customer insists keys never leave their account/HSM. Need docs on how token encryption, cache encryption, and model artifacts are wrapped with CMK.
Key rotation: customer requires annual rotation and ability to rotate without downtime. Need migration plan and how session keys are rewrapped. Include steps for rolling rewrap in POC.

Audit logging: logs must be forwarded to Splunk/SIEM in customer account or via TLS syslog. Retention policy: 7 years for certain audit trails, 1 year for request traces. Need sample CloudWatch->Kinesis->SIEM pipeline and Redwood retention controls.

Data residency: model input/output must not leave us-east-2. They will not accept cross-region fallback unless legally approved. Provide region pinning options and fallback policy that keeps data in-region.

POC acceptance criteria: synthetic workload ~500 rps (64-token average) with p95 < 250ms for text-generation; embeddings batch job of 200k docs nightly completes within 3 hours. KMS CMK wrap/unwrap validated; audit stream visible in Splunk.

Security review status: initial questionnaire answers provided 2026-01-20. Security team requested architecture diagram and KMS key policy details. Legal reviewing DPA and residency clause (redline expected).
Quote from CTO (paraphrase): 'We cannot have any customer PII traverse third-party networks — keys and audit must be under our control.'
Operational asks: support for IP allowlist rotation, a runbook for incident responses, and a verification test harness for egress IPs and latency SLOs.
Risk notes: if PrivateLink throughput is insufficient, customer is likely to request on-prem package or dedicated co-lo. Cost sensitivity exists but compliance trumps price on this account.
Next logistics: prep VPC endpoint architecture doc + example terraform; confirm static IP patterns and provide list of required security group ports by 2026-03-05.
